It also eliminates signed integer overflow undefined behavior in keypool top up.

result.summary: This PR bounds descriptor range endpoints in `ProcessDescriptorImport` and widens range calculation in `TopUpWithDB` to `int64_t`. It prevents an integer overflow and assertion abort when importing descriptors ending at 2^31 - 1 or when `-keypool` exceeds `INT32_MAX`. It also includes functional test coverage covering the crashes and the keypool refill overflow.
result.problem: When importing descriptors with an upper range endpoint of 2^31 - 1, the exclusive end computation wraps to negative numbers in `int32_t`, which writes an inverted range to disk and triggers an assertion failure in `TopUpWithDB`, terminating bitcoind. Similar crashes and signed integer overflow undefined behavior occur with extreme `-keypool` configurations or large `keypoolrefill` calls.

resolved_concerns: Missing test coverage for `keypoolrefill` overflow caught under UBSan was requested and added by the author (jeanpablojp).
Handling pre-existing corrupted records on disk and centralizing `-keypool` validation were considered and agreed to be follow-up material (molnard, shuv-amp).

categories.rationale: P2 because it fixes an assertion abort and wallet database corruption triggered by an RPC command with extreme ranges or large `-keypool` settings. Without this fix, importing a range ending at `INT32_MAX` persists an inverted descriptor record before aborting the process.

result.card: PR #35989 fixes an assertion abort and node crash in the wallet caused by integer truncation when importing descriptors with a range ending at 2^31 - 1, or when running with `-keypool` greater than `INT32_MAX`. Prior to crashing, the node persisted corrupted descriptor records with inverted ranges to the wallet database. Reviewers confirmed the bug and verified the fix across multiple scenarios with positive ACKs. The PR currently needs a rebase to resolve merge conflicts with master.
